annotations.text:
THE PROBLEM
Horizontal labels in every pane stop working past ~10 restaurants. Two rounds of geometry took the worst case 40px -> 59px and it still reads badly: 66px at twelve places is ~8 characters, so names still truncate, and staggering puts two labels one above the other near 12 and 6 o'clock where they read as one name.

Every artboard has count (8/12) and dark tweaks - flip them.

A - NUMBERED + LEGEND
Panes carry a numeral; names live in a two-column list keyed to it.

Why: a numeral is one or two glyphs, so it never truncates at any count - 8, 12 or 20. Names get full width in the list.

Cost: two places to look. The wheel no longer tells you what is on it by itself.

B - POINTER NAMES ONE
Panes are blank glass; only the pane at the pointer is named, in screen-title type above the disc.

Why: matches what the spin zoom already does - one name at a time, large. Completely count-independent.

Cost: at rest you cannot see what else is in play without spinning.

C - RADIAL LABELS
Labels run hub-to-rim along the pane bisector, flipped upright on the left half.

Why: every label gets the full radial span (~150px) regardless of count. The only form that fits real names at 12+.

Cost: breaks the handoff's own rule - labels horizontal, never rotated - and reads more fairground than Ember glass.

D - ARC + LIST
The list is the subject; the wheel is a thick glass arc breaking the right edge.

Why: names are never constrained by geometry at all, at any count. The circle motif survives as the arc.

Cost: the wheel stops being the hero of the screen - the biggest departure from the Ember drawings.
